correctness.rationale: The conditions AB=BA=B²=0 are equivalent to im B=L contained in ker A=K and ker B=H containing im A+L. These data, together with an isomorphism E/H→L, count B bijectively. The parameter δ=dim(K∩im A)=rank A−rank(A²). Standard q-subspace intersection and quotient-kernel counts give each displayed factor; the maximal-rank inequality 2b≤n−rank(A²) is sharp via an explicitly feasible intersection dimension. The included independent finite-field enumeration checks all 16 square-zero matrices at n=2,q=4, 105 at n=3,q=3, and 316 at n=4,q=2 against multiple A including nonsimilar types.

value.rationale: Counts the natural square-zero stratum inside the mutual annihilator of any fixed matrix, refining Huang’s all-annihilator count by rank and overlap. The full spectrum collapses to two elementary rank invariants even when similarity class changes, while its largest realizable rank is governed solely by rank(A²). This links two-step linear-algebra structure to an exact finite-field distribution for all dimensions and characteristics, with distinct behavior even among matrices of the same ordinary rank.
